text:
DISK FINDING, recorded here because this bead is the closest thing we have to an infrastructure home and there is no disk bead.

MEASURED at 20:00Z: nothing under /private/tmp has changed in thirty minutes, and the six large gate clones are STATIC at 3.6G, 2.8G and 2.7G x4. Free space still drifted 1.9Gi -> 1.5Gi in that window.

SO THE CLONES ARE THE STOCK, NOT THE FLOW. I implied earlier that they were the problem; they are ~17G of recoverable space, but they are not what is consuming the remaining headroom. Something else on a 926Gi volume at 100% is, and it is outside /private/tmp where I have no business looking and no way to attribute it.

That distinction matters for whoever acts on this tomorrow: deleting every abandoned clone would buy back roughly seventeen gigabytes ONCE, and would not stop the drift. Both are worth doing and they are different jobs.

My own footprint is zero -- scratchpad cleared at 19:45 and not rebuilt.

RELATED, and the reason this sits on the CI bead: a machine at 100% capacity makes every gate result untrustworthy, which is the same problem as having no CI. An agent-reported green on a full disk and an agent-reported green on a healthy one are indistinguishable in the ledger, and today the disk produced three red gates that read exactly like a colleague's code being broken.
